candidateAudit.text: Avusturya’da elektrik faturalarında yeni dönem: Aynı anda çok tüketen daha fazla ödeyecek Avusturya’da elektrik şebeke ücretlerinin hesaplanma sistemi değişiyor. 1 Ocak 2027’den itibaren başlayacak yeni modelde yalnızca ne kadar elektrik tüketildiğine değil, elektriğin ne zaman ve ne kadar yoğun kullanıldığına da bakılacak. Elektrikli otomobilini şarj ederken aynı anda ısı pompası ve yüksek tüketimli cihazları çalıştıran hanelerin şebeke maliyeti artabilecek. Tüketimini gün içine yayanlar ise tasarruf edebilecek. E-Control tarafından açıklanan yeni düzenleme, Avusturya’daki elektrik şebekelerinin daha verimli kullanılmasını ve özellikle yoğun saatlerde oluşan yükün azaltılmasını amaçlıyor. Bugüne kadar hanelerin şebeke maliyetlerinin yaklaşık yüzde 90’ı tüketilen elektrik miktarına göre hesaplanıyordu. Yeni sistemle birlikte bu yapı kademeli olarak değiştirilecek. Hedeflenen modelde şebeke ücretinin yaklaşık yüzde 50’si tüketilen elektrik miktarına, yüzde 50’si ise kullanılan güce göre belirlenecek. Aynı anda çalışan cihazlar önem kazanacak Yeni sistemde kritik nokta, bir hanenin elektrik şebekesinden aynı anda ne kadar yüksek güç çektiği olacak. Örneğin bir evde aynı anda; elektrikli otomobil şarj ediliyor, ısı pompası çalışıyor ve yüksek elektrik tüketen başka cihazlar kullanılıyorsa, kısa süre içerisinde yüksek bir tüketim zirvesi oluşabilecek. Bu durumda hanenin şebeke ücreti daha yüksek olabilir. Buna karşılık elektrikli otomobilini farklı saatlerde şarj eden, ısı pompası ve diğer yüksek tüketimli cihazlarını aynı anda çalıştırmayan tüketiciler şebeke maliyetlerini düş

candidateAudit.text: 🎹 PIANO RECITAL • SARAH COPONAT • 12.3.27 • 19:30 Die französische Pianistin und Komponistin Sarah Coponat spielt ausschließlich eigene Werke: Klaviermusik zwischen Romantik, Filmmusik und freier Improvisation. candidateAudit.title: Der chilenische Gitarrist, Sänger und Songwriter Miguel Montalban gehört zu den spannendsten Vertretern der modernen Blues-Rock-Szene. Heute in London beheimatet, verbindet er virt
candidateAudit.text: Der chilenische Gitarrist, Sänger und Songwriter Miguel Montalban gehört zu den spannendsten Vertretern der modernen Blues-Rock-Szene. Heute in London beheimatet, verbindet er virtuose Gitarrenarbeit, klassischen Rock’n’Roll und gefühlvolle Blues-Einflüsse zu einem energiegeladenen Sound, der ihn international bekannt gemacht hat. Spätestens seit seiner viralen Interpretation von Dire Straits’ „Sultans of Swing“, die weltweit Millionen Aufrufe erzielte, gilt Montalban als Ausnahmegitarrist mit außergewöhnlicher Bühnenpräsenz 2017 veröffentlichte Montalban sein Debütalbum „Guitar Juicebox“, gefolgt vom Live-Album „Live & Loud Vienna“. Mit Songs wie „Electrify“, „Last Chance“ und „Wander“ etablierte er seinen unverwechselbaren Stil zwischen Blues, Hard Rock und modernem Classic Rock. 2019 gründete er in London seine Band The Southern Vultures, die sich schnell einen Namen in der britischen Live-Szene machte. Die Kombination aus kraftvollen Grooves, virtuosen Gitarrensoli und intensiver Bühnenenergie machte die Band zu einem festen Bestandteil renommierter Clubs und Festivals. Mit dem Album „And The Southern Vultures“ sowie dem gefeierten Doppelalbum „Live in Birmingham“ festigte Montalban seinen Ruf als herausragender Performer und Songwriter. candidateAudit.text: Avusturya’da 2,40 Euro’luk paket vergisi kaldırılabilir: Hükümette anlaşmazlık Avusturya’da 1 Ekim 2026’da yürürlüğe giren ve internet alışverişlerini pahalılaştıran paket vergisi, hükümet ortakları arasında anlaşmazlığa neden oldu. ÖVP ve NEOS verginin kaldırılmasına sıcak bakarken, SPÖ bütçe gerekçesiyle uygulamanın devam etmesini istiyor. Avusturya’da yıllık yurt içi cirosu 100 milyon Euro’yu aşan büyük internet satıcılarına getirilen paket vergisi, sipariş başına 2 Euro olarak uygulanıyor. KDV ile birlikte bu tutar 2,40 Euro’ya yükseliyor. Büyük internet satış platformlarının ek maliyeti müşterilere yansıtması, uygulamanın başlamasından itibaren tepkilere yol açtı. NEOS: Vergi amacına ulaşmadı NEOS Genel Başkanı ve Dışişleri Bakanı Beate Meinl-Reisinger, yeni vergiyi sert sözlerle eleştirdi. Verginin başlangıçta Avrupa dışından gelen ucuz ürünleri hedeflediğini ancak Avusturyalı ve Avrupalı işletmeleri de etkilediğini belirten Meinl-Reisinger, uygulamayı başarısız bulduğunu söyledi. NEOS, bütçede alternatif tasarruf önlemleri bulunarak paket vergisinin kaldırılmasını talep ediyor. Başbakan Stocker değişikliğe açık Başbakan Christian Stocker de paket vergisinden memnun olmadığını belirterek, alternatif finansman önerilerini görüşmeye hazır olduklarını açıkladı. Stocker, verginin iki temel amacı bulunduğunu hatırlattı. candidateAudit.text: 🏝️ Eine ganze Insel mit Haus für nur 400.000 Euro!⁠ Vor der Küste Schottlands steht die einsame Insel Hildasay zum Verkauf. Für umgerechnet rund 400.000 Euro bekommt man 108 Hektar Land, einsame Sandstrände, zwei Süßwasserseen und eine traditionelle schottische Steinhütte mit Meerblick.⁠ ⁠ 🌊 Der Haken: Die Insel ist nur mit dem Boot erreichbar. candidateAudit.text: Come join the next Soil Session this Thursday, 17:00. You are invited to participate in the multi-channel sound installation Soil Immersion by Christian Prohammer and Johanna Unterpertinger. Following three recording sessions during the runtime of our current exhibition, your voice and sound fragments are integrated into the immersive layering of sound. Come early and catch the next exhibition tour too: starting 16:00. (Free entry, no registration) AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna About the exhibition: 03: Soil Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. The exhibition emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. candidateAudit.text: Tragödie bei Bungee-Sprung: 21-Jährige stirbt in Deutschland! Eine junge Frau aus Sachsen-Anhalt ist am Samstag bei einem Sprung in einem stillgelegten Steinbruch in Warstein (Nordrhein-Westfalen) tödlich verunglückt.⁠ ⁠ Die 21-Jährige war mit vier Begleitern vor Ort. Die Gruppe hatte die Bungee-Vorrichtung selbst gebaut, das Gelände war kein offiziell zugelassenes Kletterareal. Bei dem Sprung prallte die junge Frau gegen eine Felswand und erlitt schwerste Verletzungen.⁠ ⁠ 🚨 Trotz sofortiger Wiederbelebungsversuche starb sie noch am Unfallort. Ihre vier Begleiter standen unter Schock und wurden von Notfallseelsorgern betreut. candidateAudit.title: Today is Coming Out Day. We celebrate everyone who has come out, whether once or a hundred times. We also make room for everyone who can't, won't, or isn't ready yet. For many tran
candidateAudit.text: Today is Coming Out Day. We celebrate everyone who has come out, whether once or a hundred times. We also make room for everyone who can't, won't, or isn't ready yet. For many trans people, BIPOC queers, and folks without secure papers or family support, being visible can cost a lot. Nobody owes the world a coming out. That's why spaces like Villa Vida matter. Since 2019 we've been a living room for Vienna's queer community, a place where you don't have to explain yourself. Out, not out, still figuring it out: you belong here. Heute ist Coming Out Day. Wir feiern alle, die sich geoutet haben, ob einmal oder hundertmal. Und wir halten Platz für alle, die es nicht können, nicht wollen oder noch nicht so weit sind. Für viele trans Personen, BIPOC-Queers und Menschen ohne sicheren Aufenthalt oder Rückhalt in der Familie kann Sichtbarkeit viel kosten. Niemand schuldet der Welt ein Coming-out. Genau deshalb braucht es Orte wie die Villa Vida. Seit 2019 sind wir ein Wohnzimmer für die queere Community in Wien, ein Ort, an dem du dich nicht erklären musst. Out, nicht out oder noch am Herausfinden: Du gehörst dazu. 📍 Linke Wienzeile 102, Wien · Main entrance / Haupteingang: Spörlingasse 1 villavidacafe #VillaVida #ComingOutDay #QueerWien #QueerVienna #LGBTQIA

candidateAudit.text: Thanks for joining the opening of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ this week! At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphor. — on till 5 Nov 2026 Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 The exhibition emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). candidateAudit.title: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive na
candidateAudit.text: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive narrative obscures a deeper, more ‘errant’ truth? Media theorist and author Clemens Apprich in conversation with philosopher Jan Völker. Moderated by Amanda Holmes, Department of Philosophy, University of Applied Arts Vienna Welcome: Ulrike Kuch, Rector of the University of Applied Arts Vienna A cooperation of the department of Media Theory and the department of Philosophy. ‘Errant Intelligence’ challenges the prevailing biological and individualistic interpretations of machine learning, arguing instead for a radical understanding of machine intelligence. The book embraces the deviations, inconsistencies, and ‘errant behaviour’ as fundamental to the discovery of new knowledge, moving beyond the illusion of mere optimisation. Drawing on media theory, cybernetics, and a unique psychoanalytic lens, it explores the ‘technological unconscious’ of machine learning. It traces the historical roots of AI, from early automatons and the Turing machine to natural language processing and contemporary machine learning systems. Challenging the idea of an autonomous, self-generating AI, the book exposes the hidden labour, assumed logics, and inherent biases that animate its operation. It re-evaluates computational thinking, insisting on its inherently social, collective, and symbolic character, and revealing how language and logical paradoxes are not obstacles but constitutive forces that shape intelligent machines

candidateAudit.text: In this workshop with Helena Detsch we will explore simple ways to create a fascinating natural color palette from soil and plant-based materials like earths, minerals, vegetables, kitchen supplies and algae pigments. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ Duration: 15:30–17:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio (free entry) Together, we'll first experiment with making self-made oil- or watercolors from 100% natural sources and then explore the many possibilities of sustainable painting, discovering how these self-made colors behave on paper and fabric and what a truly organic painting practice can look like. candidateAudit.text: About the next exhibition at AIL: Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. What is happening beneath our feet? At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. With contributions by: Franziska Allerberger (Geographer), Michael Bahn (Ecologist), Helena Detsch (Visual Artist), Cornelia Dirnberger (Visual Artist), Christian Prohammer (Musician, Audio Engineer), Nora Schöpfer (Visual Artist), Konstantina Maria Serjannis (Cultural Scientist), Johanna Unterpertinger (Musician) ’03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). candidateAudit.text: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Applied Photography and Time-Based Media at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, which explores the synergistic potential of student teams from different degree programs. In collaboration with the department Industrial Design, this year’s focus was on the intersection of photography and the object, with particular attention paid to the relationship with set design, styling, casting and narrative. Seen from the perspective of Applied Photography, the object and thus the chair, is a welcome protagonist. Photography’s multiple applied genres are cited here: documentary, fashion, advertising, architecture and the portrait. When the function in Industrial Design coalesces with the idea of the purpose in Applied Photography, the question of factuality emerges. Be not mistaken: The most literal things are often the most confusing and enigmatic. Between what it is and how it is*, worlds unfold. We put the images to work. VDW Cocktail: 29 Sep, 17:00–18:00 Showcase and drinks followed by a collective walk to the billboards in front of the main entrance of the University Open Saturdays: 26 Sep / 3 Oct, 11:00–18:00 Opening hours: Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna The collaborative works are on display at the AIL and on the billboards at the university’s main entrance on Oskar-Kokoschka-Platz. dieangewandte viennadesignweek applied.photography angewandte_id Feat

candidateAudit.text: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is delighted to once again host one event in the program. unsafeandsounds AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna (Free entry) Overview: 18:30 Panel Discussion, unsafe+sounds in cooperation with the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures (University of Applied Arts Vienna) weibel.institute Affective Histories Timotheus Vermeulen and Christian Höller in conversation with Sophie Publig History is never simply given. It is made through the scales and materials by which the past becomes legible: from sweeping narratives and historical events to gestures, sounds, images, technical infrastructures, and seemingly minor traces SOPHIE PUBLIG is a Senior Scientist researching digital ecosystems. Based at the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, she navigates the intricate networks of online territories. TIMOTHEUS VERMEULEN is Professor of Media, Culture and Society at the University of Oslo and joint director of the Media Aesthetics Research Group. He was a visiting scholar in Art History at Harvard in 2023–24 and will serve as joint Principal Investigator on a project on the politics of tone at the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo in 2027–28. candidateAudit.text: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developing the project's multisensory scenography – the so-called SΫS SPACE. Aim of the Summer Studio is to prepare the prototype of the scenography, which will be established at the AIL in June 2027 as the centerpiece of the final exhibition of the PEEK project ’SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS — Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness.’ The SΫS SPACE facilitates a physical experience of one's own embededdness within living systems, within complex interrelationships – within a greater whole. It paves the way for relational sensing and thinking – an embodied systems awareness, that can help in coping with complexity, challenges, and uncertainties, and in making good decisions towards sustainable futures. It deliberately reduces the dominance of the sense of sight, placing the emphasis instead on smell, touch, and hearing. Numerous scientists, as well as invited artists, politicians, journalists, children, senior citizens, curators, cultural workers, educators, and teenagers are individually guided through the immersive environment by Jeanette Müller and Paul Divjak and share their responses in photo-based reflections and semi-structured interviews. Their feedback directly informs the prototype. Save the date! 14 and 15 Sep 2026 The SΫS SPACE will open to the public in individual time slots for an exclusive multisensory experience. candidateAudit.text: Every drag performance tells a story. candidateAudit.text: Over the past season, every spin, every step, and every dance has made a real difference. 💜 Thanks to your generosity, Queer Salsa Wien has raised over €850 for the Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund (QVMAF) this year already. The Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund provides one-off emergency microgrants to queer people in Vienna experiencing unexpected financial hardship. Whether someone is struggling to pay rent, buy groceries, cover medical costs, or get through another crisis, these grants help community members when they need it most. A huge thank you to the incredible Queer Salsa Wien team for organising these classes, and to everyone who has danced, donated, volunteered, and supported this initiative. Every donation, no matter the size, helps build a stronger community based on solidarity and mutual care. Queer Salsa classes will be back at Villa Vida in October but in the meantime you can join their outdoor classes and parties. Follow queersalsawien for information. The Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund is an initiative started by hint.wien and villavidacafe. If you’d like to learn more about the Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund or make a donation, visit queervienna.at. candidateAudit.text: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. Across these artistic approaches, [REVERBERATED] invites visitors to consider memory not as something simply preserved, but as something continuously produced through interactions between bodies, technologies, and environments. The exhibition thus explores how the past continues to reverberate within the systems of the present. With contributions by: Agustina Belén Agüero, Lobna Awidat, Phin Anibal, Rimon Alyagon Darr, Ronnie Danaher, Tatiana Del Valle, Hasti Ghasedi, Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz, Hanna Hofmann, Tal Horesh, Mauritius Itzinger, Laura Isselhorst, Dina Karaman, Moritz Klarer, Anna Buchner, Leonard Otterbein, David Ristić, Rajarshi Sarkar, Agnes Schyberg, Aryan Shahabian, Majedeh Shahvelayati, Mehrta Shirzadian, Pauline Simon, Laura Chalabi, People of Soil Photos: Lea Dörl

candidateAudit.text: A new series of postcards is now installed at Café Exchange cafe_exchange The series was extracted from the course ‘Drawing: Here & Now’ by Simon Goritschnig zeichnungunddruckgrafik In collaborative drawing, two people share a single pen – the line becomes a space of negotiation. A play between control and letting go. Who leads – and when? Impulse meets resistance, conviction meets empathy. Not always a conversation, but always an understanding – a dance on paper. These and other experiments are part of the course “Drawing: Here & Now” by Simon Goritschnig, in which students of the department Drawing and Printmaking explore various qualities of drawing beyond observational study. In the project “Reflex,” these experimental setups are set against observational drawing. Students draw in the cashier hall of the former Postsparkasse, intuitively picking up details from architecture and space, as well as situations of coming together: conversations, movements, gazes. In this process, it becomes visible how public and social space is visually probed and explored. The focus lies on reflection — with, through, and within drawing. With contributions by: Andrea Vairelles, Anna Marino, Beth Sorby, Emilia Schönwiese, Flora Schmid, Hannah Horn, Henriette Sonntag, Leo Hasslinger, Maria Lutkova, Max Offergeld, Nikolaus Kohout, Sophie Schweizer, Anija S Dartizio, Timo Pfeifer, Vera Kügel AIL in cooperation with the department Drawing and Printmaking and Simon Goritschnig Image: Henriette Sonntag Design: Atelier Dreibholz Concept Postcard Editions and Production: Eva Weber

candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 4 Jul 2026, 15:00 The Geography of Yellow Walls Performance by Mehrta Shirzadian mehrrta Bright yellow becomes a quiet declaration of care, resistance, and return. Here, the body is reclaimed as homeland, shaped by experience rather than imposed borders. A performance unfolding through turmeric as healing material and the body as living territory. The work is rooted in a deep commitment to women’s health and critical scientific perspectives, engaging forms of embodied knowledge that have long been ignored or erased. The body becomes both evidence and memory, offering its own geography as a space of protection, defiance, and belonging. The performance is adapted to each site, responding to the spatial and contextual conditions of different venues. Mehrta Shirzadian is a performance and multimedia artist and artistic ­researcher working at the intersection of art and science. With a background in molecular biology, mathematics, and computer science, she creates participatory works exploring microbial life, sound, and bodily ecologies, addressing embodiment, agency, and the politics of representation. Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. candidateAudit.title: On view till Saturday (18:00) – An installation presented by the department of Digital Arts / Part of Angewandte Festival René’s Collapse Collection’ is a fictional startup and alt
candidateAudit.text: On view till Saturday (18:00) – An installation presented by the department of Digital Arts / Part of Angewandte Festival René’s Collapse Collection’ is a fictional startup and alternative investment platform that explores the cultural, economic, and emotional afterlife of the collapse of René Benko’s SIGNA empire. Through NFTs, merchandise, video works, and performative sales strategies, the project examines how value is produced through speculation, narrative, and collective belief. Originally developed through public interventions, the project was expanded through a student take over by Digitale Kunst. This exhibition presents new project strands developed by the students: an NFT series reflecting on financial dependency, a merchandise collection appropriating the aesthetics of startup culture and luxury branding, and a series of short-form videos combining influencer culture, promotional performance, and social commentary. Operating at the intersection of installation, performance, and participatory fiction, Renés Collapse Collection invites visitors to engage directly with the mechanisms of speculation, value production, and collapse. A project by by Zora Hünermann and Jakob Margit With contributions by: Ulrike Fritzsche, Koschka Cosmo Keye, Juarez Suarez, Ghanishka Kedar, Sei Jeung, Ghazal Naeimi, Dongjoo Kim, Jazzmin, Margherita Pruneti, Nicolás Henao Bonnet, Roma Bogdanov, and Grisha Terno.

candidateAudit.text: In a world that is seemingly always connected, we lose ourselves in constant contact. As part of Angewandte Festival, AIL presents: Sich zusammen schreiben [to get in touch], A performance and poem by Carla Schwering and Timna Lugstein from by the department of Institute of Fine Arts & Media Art – Photography (Sophie Thun) The phrase "Schreiben wir uns zusammen" that on the surface means something like “let’s write to each other again in more detail” actually implies a postponement. In the performance, the artists type excerpts from their shared chat history in a poetic arrangement on two typewriters facing each other – messages in which they attempt to get closer to one another. The time and effort spent cancelling meet ups, for which there is supposedly no capacity is made visible. With the postcards created for the performance, visitors can reconnect with a long-lost friend. On the occasion of Angewandte Festival AIL hosts a selection of performances and installations in the cashier hall and the current exhibition will have more activations. We will give you an overview, step by step AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna

candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 Jul 2026, 15:30 Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) Performance by Leonard Otterbein leonard.ottb The audio performance Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) explores how sound can model processes of memory formation and transformation. Layered oscillations and brief sound textures repeat with phase shifts, gradually overlapping and partially canceling each other out, much like the traces in an overwritten manuscript. The work is inspired by memory research on reconsolidation – in which recalling an event alters its stored form – and its cultural studies counterpart, reconstructivity. The piece is composed of multiple layers of sound that continuously overlap anew, attempting to cancel each other out in the process. In this process, however, the layers are never completely erased, so that fragments of the preceding states always remain Leonard Otterbein is a sound artist and composer with a background in ecology and ecotoxicology, where he studied mixture effects of agricultural pesticides and nanoparticles. His work spans instrumental and electroacoustic composition, examining perceptual thresholds. He works with psychoacoustic effects and approaches sound as spatial and sculptural material shaped by its relation to space. Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. candidateAudit.title: From the project SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS. Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness – a performance by mueller_divjak in front of Otto Wagner Postsp
candidateAudit.text: From the project SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS. Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness – a performance by mueller_divjak in front of Otto Wagner Postsparkasse as part of Angewandte Festival! 'LIMINAL TRACES. Celebrating Acoustic Ecologies' is a dynamic sound lecture that understands the acoustic world as a phenomenon of resonance, shaped by connectedness and interaction. Through the live-curated interplay of field recordings, physical and digital artefacts, the performance traces sonic imprints deeply embedded in our collective memory, presenting them as a new listening experience. Developed within SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS at the AIL, this solar performance explores the intersections of sound, pop history and solar energy, celebrating concept, improvisation and the (unexpected) emergent. The performance ends when the energy collected by the mobile solar unit runs out. — The artist and researcher duo MUELLER-DIVJAK (Dr. Jeanette Müller and Dr. Paul Divjak), who conceived and initiated SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS, is working since 2023 at AIL with international artists and systems scientists to form experiential spaces by artistic means (scenographies) and to create sensory impressions that help us to better understand and resonate with living systems. During the project essential principles of living systems are transformed into olfactory, auditory and tactile artworks / artefacts and used experimentally. Team: Jeanette Müller, Paul Divjak, Alexandra Graupner, Anna-Maria Irgang

candidateAudit.title: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 July 2026, 15:00 Hypervigilant Performance by Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz iukumukui Part of the exhibition [RE
candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 July 2026, 15:00 Hypervigilant Performance by Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz iukumukui Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory artscience.ak Constant vigilance can develop as a response to racial discrimination and transgenerational trauma, allowing potential threats to be recognized in advance. This fight-or-flight state activates the nervous system and can lead to chronic muscle tension and bruxism. Teeth grinding occurs as a way of coping with stress during sleep, often driven by societal expectations to suppress fear or anger. Hypervigilant addresses this suppressed anger. Aluminum teeth suspended from the ceiling form a space similar to a cage that oscillates between protection and exposure. Shaped as gong-like instruments, the oversized representation of the artist’s bite is set into vibration during a sound performance to release embodied pressure and reduce tension in the nervous system. Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz’s practice centers on suppressed experiences expressed in imagined worlds. Through performative sculptures and installations, she examines spatial dynamics and power structures. Addressing socio-political themes such as racism, sexism, gender, and sexuality, she builds subconscious environments using reference-based objects and constructions in combination with text and sound. Es ist ein Raum für echte Begegnung, in dem Gesundheit, Körperarbeit und menschliche Verbindung im Mittelpunkt stehen. Wir suchen Verstärkung! Unser Team besteht nicht nur aus Experten, sondern vor allem aus Herzensmenschen und Freunden, die eine gemeinsame Vision teilen. Um unser Angebot im Bereich sportliche Bewegung zu erweitern, suchen wir motivierte Trainer:innen, die unsere Leidenschaft für Dynamik, Kraft und Technik teilen. Du passt perfekt zu uns, wenn du Classes leitest in: = Yoga = Pilates = Functional Training & Mobility = Somatic Movement Was dich bei uns erwartet: Bei uns findest du nicht nur ein wunderschönes Studio mit klassischem Wiener Altbau-Charme. Dich erwartet ein Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt und gemeinsam wachsen möchte. Wir bieten dir den idealen Kraftplatz, um deine Impulse zu setzen und Menschen auf ihrem Weg zu mehr Wohlbefinden zu begleiten. Bewirb dich jetzt! Hast du Lust, Teil unserer Medicina-Familie zu werden? Dann schreib uns einfach an office@medicina.wien – wir freuen uns darauf, dich und deine Vision kennenzulernen! 🤍 Medicina Studio | Lerchenfelder Straße, 1070 Wien
